title: Contextual Combinatorial Bandits with Changing Action Sets via Gaussian Processes

strengths: The combination of contextual information, combinatorial constraints, changing arm availability, and semi-bandit feedback addresses a useful problem with an identifiable audience in bandit learning and resource allocation.

The algorithm clearly combines GP confidence bounds with an approximation oracle. Lemma 2 provides a convincing reduction from super-arm regret to posterior uncertainty, and the arrival-dependent information-gain measure offers a useful perspective.

The experiments examine data-derived contexts, varying correlation lengths, and sparse approximation tradeoffs. Repeated runs, variability plots, runtime measurements, pseudocode, and a source-code link help readers assess and potentially reproduce the findings.
weaknesses: Necessary theoretical correction: The lower bound in Theorem 3, restated as Theorem 6, is false for the stated arbitrary feasible-action families. For example, take T=K=1, X={a,b}, only {a} feasible, noise variance 1, and kernel matrix diag(0.01,1). The feasible information gain is 0.5 log(1.01), whereas the unrestricted γ_1 is 0.5 log 2. Equation (A33) unjustifiably replaces feasible sequences with arbitrary context selections. Additional feasibility assumptions or a revised statement are needed. Equation (A34) also uses posterior variances after observing the current point, whereas the information-gain identity requires the preceding variances.

Necessary proof clarification: Lemma 3 treats adaptively selected contexts as a fixed Gaussian design. A deterministic oracle still selects random contexts through its dependence on noisy observations; z_t is not determined by previous selected contexts alone. Consequently, the entropy equalities in (A11)–(A12) require more careful conditioning and expectations. A pathwise block-determinant argument appears capable of repairing the main regret analysis, but the supplied justification is incomplete.

Necessary clarification of application scope: Gaussian latent means with additive Gaussian observations do not directly cover the Bernoulli activation model used in MovieLens. The manuscript should identify this as an empirical application outside the guarantees and explain how UCB values are converted into valid probabilities for TIM+. It should also distinguish the three-movie budget from the theoretical K, which counts selected base arms, here edges. In crowdsourcing, specify the noise distribution and any clipping: under Gaussian noise, log(1+sum r_i) is undefined with positive probability and does not satisfy the stated global reward assumptions.

Necessary experimental clarification: Simulation III calls exp(-||x-x'||/(2l²)) a squared-exponential kernel, although that kernel requires a squared norm. This changes the sampled functions' regularity and the interpretation of the correlation experiment. Specify the actual generating and learning kernels and whether the learner's lengthscale changes with the generating lengthscale. Also reconcile the 250-versus-300-round descriptions and the inducing-point lists with the plotted configurations.

Necessary qualification of claims: MovieLens and Foursquare supply contexts or graph structure, while outcomes are generated from prescribed functions. These experiments support conclusions about the specified simulations. Near equality with an approximate oracle benchmark does not establish optimal performance. Likewise, Table 1 compares different function-class assumptions, so its rates do not establish an unconditional improvement over prior methods. Claims of tightness, real-world superiority, and broad online scalability should be narrowed to what the analysis and experiments establish.

Optional improvements: Comparing against an exact GP implementation with incremental matrix-factorization updates would make the runtime comparison more informative. Additional kernel-misspecification sensitivity experiments would strengthen the practical conclusions. These extensions are secondary to correcting the theoretical statements and clarifying the existing experiments.
